content.text:
Done. Three PNGs are in the working folder, rendered from a single `card.html` that adapts via aspect-ratio media queries.

**Output**
| File | Size | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `square.png` | 1080×1080 | Stacked: header → portrait+name row → title → footer |
| `landscape.png` | 1920×1080 | Two columns: text left, 440px portrait right |
| `story.png` | 1080×1920 | Vertical: portrait above name, title, stacked footer |

**How it's built**
- `@font-face` loads the local `Inter.ttf` as a variable font (`font-weight: 100 900`), confirmed applied rather than falling back.
- One set of CSS custom properties (`--pad`, `--portrait`, `--title`, …) is overridden per breakpoint, so each size is retuned rather than just scaled — the landscape moves the portrait into its own column, the story stacks the footer so the pill button never crowds the date line.
- Portrait is a fixed square box with `border-radius: 50%` + `object-fit: cover` and `object-position: 50% 42%` to keep the face centered in the crop at every size; a violet ring and soft halo tie it to the accent color.
- Title uses `text-wrap: balance` so the long sentence breaks into even lines (3 lines on square/landscape, 4 on story) instead of leaving a stranded word.

**Verification** — I ran a headless Playwright audit on all three viewports checking: document scroll size vs. viewport (no overflow), every element's bounding box inside the frame, `scrollWidth > clientWidth` text clipping, pairwise overlap of all text/image boxes, and that each portrait's box is exactly square with `border-radius: 50%`. All three passed with zero defects, and I also reviewed the rendered PNGs directly.

One judgement call worth flagging: I enlarged the landscape portrait (400→440px) and the story portrait/title (330→376px, 76→84px) after the first pass, because the initial renders were technically correct but left noticeably dead space. That was my own call on visual balance, not a defect fix — easy to revert in the `:root` overrides if you prefer the airier version.
